Reading the Q4 strategy document.

NEXUS CORP — Q4 STRATEGIC INITIATIVES

Revenue Acceleration Program. Q4 is the highest-stakes quarter of the fiscal year. The board has approved a revenue acceleration program anchored on three priorities: closing the two enterprise deals currently in contract review (estimated combined ARR of $4.2M), launching the Professional tier at $299/month to capture the large under-served mid-market segment, and executing the regional expansion into the Pacific Northwest with two new account executives starting October 15.

Product Milestone: Platform V3.0. The Q4 engineering roadmap has a single load-bearing milestone: the launch of Platform V3.0 during the third week of November. V3.0 introduces real-time collaboration features (co-editing, presence awareness, comment threads), the redesigned analytics dashboard requested by twelve enterprise accounts, and the API v2 gateway that three partner integrations depend on. Any slip in V3.0 launch affects the enterprise contract closings and the Professional tier pricing story simultaneously.

Cost Management. Operating expenditure in Q4 is budgeted at $8.1M against a Q3 actuals baseline of $7.8M. The $300k increase is entirely attributed to the new account executives, expanded cloud capacity for V3.0 launch traffic, and the customer advisory board event planned for mid-November. No discretionary spend is authorized outside this allocation; all requests above $5k require VP approval via the procurement system. The finance team will conduct weekly burn reviews starting October 1.

Customer Success Initiatives. Two structured programs run in Q4: the Enterprise Health Sprint targets the seven accounts flagged as churn risks after Q3 NPS scoring below 30, and the Expansion Motion program works with sales to convert twenty-two under-utilized accounts, targeting $650k in expansion revenue.

Legal and Compliance. Thomas Wren has flagged two time-sensitive items: updated data processing agreements required by three EU-based enterprise customers before their November renewal dates, and the SOC 2 Type II audit fieldwork scheduled for the first two weeks of October.

The Q4 strategy has four main areas:
1. Revenue Acceleration: Close two enterprise deals ($4.2M ARR combined), launch Professional tier at $299/month, expand to Pacific Northwest (2 new AEs, Oct 15).
2. Platform V3.0 Launch: Third week of November. Real-time collaboration, redesigned analytics dashboard, API v2 gateway. A delay affects both enterprise closings.
3. Cost Management: $8.1M Q4 budget; VP approval required for requests above $5k; weekly burn reviews.
4. Customer Success + Compliance: Enterprise Health Sprint (7 at-risk accounts), Expansion Motion ($650k target), EU DPA renewals, and SOC 2 audit in early October.
Read 'q4-risks' and summarize the top risks.
Reading the Q4 risk register.

NEXUS CORP — Q4 RISK REGISTER

Risk 1 — V3.0 Schedule Slippage (probability: HIGH, impact: CRITICAL). The Platform V3.0 launch is scheduled for the third week of November, a fixed commitment made to two enterprise prospects during contract negotiations. The engineering team's current velocity estimate puts the collaboration feature set six to nine days behind the internal target. If the delay exceeds ten days, the launch slips into December, which conflicts with the customer advisory board and creates a credibility problem with both enterprise deals. Mitigation: Engineering leadership has approved a two-sprint scope reduction — the comment-thread feature will ship as a follow-up patch in early December rather than at V3.0 launch — buying eight days of schedule recovery. Owner: Rafael Torres. Weekly review cadence from October 6.

Risk 2 — Enterprise Deal Slippage (probability: MEDIUM, impact: HIGH). Deal A ($2.4M ARR, 3-year term) is blocked on HIPAA BAA legal review. Deal B ($1.8M ARR, 18-month term) is awaiting payment-terms negotiation with prospect's finance team. Both remain in-forecast for Q4 close.

Risk 3 — SOC 2 Audit Finding (probability: LOW, impact: HIGH). Privileged-access review cadence was not updated from quarterly to monthly as required; compensating control documentation is being prepared proactively. Affects three EU customers with SOC 2 as a renewal condition.

Risk 4 — New AE Ramp Time (probability: MEDIUM, impact: MEDIUM). Pacific Northwest AEs start October 15 and won't be pipeline-productive until week 6. Regional revenue target of $380k depends on a deal closing by December 31. Mitigation: pre-assigning two sales-ready prospects on day one.

Top Q4 risks:
1. V3.0 Slippage (High/Critical): 6-9 days behind; scope reduction on comment threads buys 8 days back.
2. Enterprise Deal Slippage (Medium/High): Deal A blocked on HIPAA BAA; Deal B on payment terms. Both in-forecast.
3. SOC 2 Audit Gap (Low/High): Privileged-access cadence gap; compensating controls prepared. Affects three EU renewals.
